To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Th2 cell‐derived cytokines promote the accumulation of ILCs in the lung by a mechanism involving the ILC2‐autonomous activation of STAT6.
Th2‐derived IL‐13/IL‐4 promote ILC2 proliferation by STAT6 signaling in ILC2 in the lung.
IL‐4 and IL‐13 produced from Th2 cells are required for ILC2 proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of ILCs during helminth infection.
the regulation of the proliferation and accumulation of ILCs in the lung.
the role of the Th2 cell‐derived cytokine IL‐4/ IL‐13 in the regulation of ILC 2 accumulation in the mouse lung during an acute helminth infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Th2 cells are required for ILC2 accumulation by promoting their proliferation and survival in the lung during a type 2 immune responses.
the Th2 cell‐derived cytokine IL‐4/13 promotes ILC2 accumulation and proliferation in the lung by a direct effect on the ILC2s themselves.
Th2 cells promote ILC2 proliferation via IL‐4/13 and STAT6 signaling in ILC2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Th2 cells promote ILC2 expansion in the lung by a STAT6 signaling in ILC2 cells.
ILC2 accumulation during helminth infection is driven by IL‐4/13‐mediated STAT6 signaling in the ILC2s and that the STAT6 pathway can be targeted to reduce ILC2 accumulation.
Th2 cells are important in promoting ILC2 accumulation during an acute type‐2 immune response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Th2‐derived cytokines promote ILC2 proliferation during helminth infection and that this effect is at least partially mediated by STAT6 signaling in ILC2 cells.
IL‐4 and IL‐13 produced from T‐helper cells can promote ILC2 proliferation.
IL‐4 and IL‐13 signaling via STAT6 is required in ILC2 for their proliferation during an acute type‐2 immune response.
